findings.title: ThrowConstructorNonCallableError called before validating target_node is a JSFunction
findings.message: In `BuildCallWithFeedback`, when the feedback cell indicates a class constructor, `BuildCallRuntime(Runtime::kThrowConstructorNonCallableError, {target_node})` is invoked before `BuildCheckJSFunction(target_node)` or the feedback-cell reference check. This means `target_node` may not be a JSFunction at all when passed to `ThrowConstructorNonCallableError`. The runtime call internally casts its argument to `JSFunction`, triggering a DCHECK failure when the actual runtime value does not match that type (e.g., the slot was primed with a class constructor C1 but is subsequently called with a different non-JSFunction value).
findings.suggestion: Move the `IsClassConstructor` check to AFTER `BuildCheckJSFunction` and `BuildCheckValueByReference` so that `target_node` is guaranteed to be the expected JSFunction (with matching SFI and feedback cell) before it is passed to `ThrowConstructorNonCallableError`.

ground_truth.root_cause: The class-constructor early-return path was inserted BEFORE the `BuildCheckJSFunction` and `BuildCheckValueByReference` guards. Those guards normally deoptimize if `target_node` is not the expected JSFunction, but they are bypassed when the feedback indicates a class constructor. As a result, an arbitrary value can reach `ThrowConstructorNonCallableError`, which unconditionally treats it as a JSFunction.
